text.content:
• What a minion is: a foe who goes down in one blow and comes in crowds. A minion has 1 HP; its attacks and Level are unchanged (Monsters & Treasure, Building Encounters). Any creature can be run as a minion. Goblins, kobolds, orcs, hobgoblins, gnolls, skeletons and zombies are the usual ones; the creatures in this chapter include minions made for it.
  • Going down: any damage drops a minion: a hit, half damage on a save, a splash, an aura.
  • Cleaving through: when a weapon hit drops a minion and the damage was at least twice its Level, the hit also drops one more minion of the same kind: one within your reach for a melee attack, or one in a straight line beyond the target for a ranged one.
  • Sharing a turn: minions of the same kind act together on one turn. They can all move, then all attack.
  • Group attack: up to five minions of the same kind that can reach the same target can attack together. Roll once, with Advantage only if every one of them has it. On a hit, each minion that joined deals its damage.
  • Group saves: when many minions of the same kind save against the same effect, roll once for each group of up to five.
  • Morale: minions check as one group. They check when the first of them falls and again when half are down, using the Codex's Morale Check. A leader who can be seen and heard lets them roll with Advantage.
  • Budget: five minions count as one creature of their Level; eight from Level 5, ten from Level 9. Minions ignore the crowd rule.
  • How many: ten to twenty in a fight up to 10th level, twenty to thirty above it, usually with a few ordinary creatures or a leader beside them. Fewer than one creature's worth isn't worth the bother.
  • Tell your players: fights with minions play best when the players know the rules above before the dice come out.

• The rules: a retainer is a henchman who sought you out, run in Chapter 2's simplified frame, with its signature attack landing when you hit (Fighting together).
  • In encounters: a party with retainers is stronger than its number. Treat each retainer like a powerful magic item: a fight that would be hard for the party alone is right for the party and its retainers, and a deadly one is merely hard.

A role says how a creature fights, not how strong it is. Most fights are better with two or three roles than with five of one kind.

RoleHow it fightsBest beside
AmbusherHides before and during the fight, strikes from coverSoldiers, controllers
ArtilleryKeeps its distance and shootsSoldiers, minions
BruteLots of HP, hits hard, charges inControllers, leaders
ControllerMoves, hinders and blinds foes, works areasBrutes, soldiers
LeaderFights with a crew and makes it better (below)Minions and anyone
MinionDies in one blow, wins by numbersLeaders, artillery
SkirmisherHits and runs, picks off the weakAny
SoldierArmoured, holds foes in placeArtillery, ambushers
SoloA fight for a whole party on its ownNothing, or a few minions
SupportHeals, buffs and moves its alliesBrutes, soldiers

• Solos: a solo follows Monsters & Treasure: two turns a round, Shaking it off, Bloodied, and three villain actions (opener, crowd control, ultimate), the opener dealing damage on top of its control.
  • Leaders: a leader is a boss who fights with a crew rather than alone: an ordinary creature, usually 1 or 2 Levels above the party, with a Command that works once per round, out of turn, straight after one of its allies' turns. A fight has one leader at most. Kill it, and its crew checks Morale at once.
  • Moving the boss: a boss that stands still dies. Give it a way to move: flight, burrowing, a ledge to jump to, minions to hide behind.

A boss is best met at home. A lair is a short dungeon, three to six areas, built around its master.

  • Every area has a job: a fight with the boss's servants, a hazard, a trap, a puzzle or a clue to the boss's weakness. Not every area has a fight.
  • The boss's chamber: put the boss's advantages in the room, not in its stat block: high ground, cover, a chasm, things to knock over, a pool it can swim into. The players should be able to use them too.
  • Warning signs: what the players find on the way in should tell them what they face and how dangerous it is, so they can prepare or walk away.
  • Servants: the boss's servants fight in the rooms before it, or come running when it calls. Minions are best for this.
  • The hoard: the boss keeps its treasure in the lair (its treasure code), with one Unique item from Monsters & Treasure and one reward that isn't gold: a map, a recipe, a secret, a title.

Frogfolk of marsh, jungle river and flooded ruin, damp-skinned and poisonous to touch. Left alone they are peaceable, and they would rather vanish into the reeds than fight. Their waters fouled, they turn vicious.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Angulotl Tadpole, Angulotl Blade, Angulotl Needler, Angulotl Seer.

Cat-sized lesser kin of the dragons, rare even where they are found. The metallic dragons of Depsopteron's east breed or teach them; they share the dragons' blood but little of their mind or magic, and no true dragon counts them as its own. They nose out magic, sense lies told in Draconic, and are prized as companions by wizards who can win their trust. They seldom fight unless cornered.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Dragonet.

A worm the length of a river barge, its mouth a ring of grinding plates, with three long tongues that whip out from the ground to drag prey down. It hunts by feel, rising under anything heavy enough to shake the earth.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Kingfissure Worm.

A great cat whose mane drinks the light and throws it back as false images. It is never quite where it seems to be, and its two tails crack with stolen sunlight.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Lightbender.

Goblins fight in swarms, and a clever goblin boss keeps it that way: plenty of runners up front, the boss well behind them.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Goblin Runner, Goblin Warlord.

Kobolds who have learned to fight like a legion: interlocked shields at the front, traps on every flank.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Kobold Shieldbearer, Kobold Trapmaster.

Orc raiders fight to prove themselves before their chief, and the chief leads from the front.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Orc Raider, Orc Warchief.

Hobgoblins fight as they drill, and they drill every day. A legion's captain moves its soldiers like pieces on a board.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Hobgoblin Legionnaire, Hobgoblin War Captain.

The gnoll clans loyal to Yeenoghu, the gnoll demon lord, still haunt Ellonmyr in Aldori after the Shattering. His touch is on them: lean, laughing and always hungry. Each kill drives the pack wilder.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Gnoll Ravager, Gnoll Fang of the Pit.

The walking dead in their hundreds, and the one who herds them.

In the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium: Grave Shambler, Corpse Herder.
